questions.text: "___ country in the study showed some health improvement." (100%, singular, individually)
"___ treatments were tested in the trial, and ___ showed promising results." (two treatments, both)
"___ of the two medications worked for this patient — surgery is now required." (not one, not the other)
questions.hint: "Neither of" = not one and not the other

questions.text: "There is ___ research supporting this claim." (very small amount, almost none, negative)
"___ studies have confirmed the link between sleep and cognitive performance." (some, positive)
"___ adults get the recommended seven to nine hours of sleep — most get significantly less." (almost none)
"___ evidence supports the use of this supplement." (large formal amount, positive)
questions.hint: "A great deal of" = formal large amount + uncountable

questions.text: "___ of the patients was given a personalised treatment plan." (individually, one by one)
"___ stress is healthy — a small amount improves focus." (small amount, positive)
"You can choose ___ therapy — both approaches are effective for your condition." (one or the other)
What is described as the "double burden of disease"?
opts: Having two doctors for one patient
Both communicable and non-communicable diseases in the same population
The financial cost of treating illness
Two peaks in global disease rates
questions.correct: Both communicable and non-communicable diseases in the same population

questions.text: "___ rest ___ vulnerability seems valued in this workplace." (neither is valued)
questions.hint: "Neither... nor" = not one and not the other

questions.text: "How ___ patients visited the clinic last month?" (countable)
What does the text on mental health say is the main barrier to treatment?
opts: Stigma — the social shame associated with mental illness
questions.correct: Stigma — the social shame associated with mental illness
questions.hint: Reading 2: "stigma is perhaps the most powerful barrier"

questions.text: "___ single person in the group completed the full health assessment." (100%, emphatic)
"___ of us can be truly healthy in isolation." (not anyone at all)
Which sentence uses a quantifier correctly in formal writing?
opts: Lots of research has been done.
A large number of studies confirm this finding.
questions.correct: A large number of studies confirm this finding.
questions.hint: "A large number of" = formal; other options are informal

questions.text: What did the Harvard study find was the strongest predictor of late-life health?
questions.hint: Listening 3B: Dr. Petrov quotes the Harvard study

questions.text: "___ the doctor and the patient agreed — communication is essential in healthcare."
"___ information about this treatment is available to the public." (very small amount, uncountable)
"___ of the participants chose the same treatment option." (100% as a group, with "of")
questions.hint: "All of" + the + noun = 100% as a group

questions.text: A state of physical and emotional exhaustion caused by prolonged work stress is called ___.
"She slept ___ night without interruption." (= the complete, unbroken night)
"Few patients improved" and "A few patients improved" have the same meaning.
